Department of Computer Science and Applications,  DST-Centre  for Policy Research, DPIIT-IPR 
Chair at Panjab University (PU), Chandigarh in collaboration  with Knowledgentia Consultants, 
New Delhi a women cofounded law firm organized a national semina r to celebrate the World 
Intellectual Property Day on 26th April 2023 (Wednesday) at Panja b University, Chandigarh. The 
theme of the event was “Women and IP: Accelerating Innovation a nd Creativity”. The event aimed 
to bring together eminent people in society including domain exper ts, members of academia and 
key stakeholders on a common platform for understanding the role, co ntribution and challenged 
women face in the field of IP.  Registrar of the Panj ab University, Chandigarh Prof. Y.P Verma 
inaugurated the event and mentioned about contribution of women in th e filed of IP over the years. 
He highlighted the initiatives undertaken by Panjab University in contributing towards IP such as  
DPIIT-IPR chair, CIIP centre. Sitting Judge of Panjab and H aryana High court Hon’ble Mr. Justice 
Aman Chaudhary graced the event as chief guest. He highlight ed the contribution of women in IP at 
various platforms as well as praised the innovative thinking wome n bring in various domains. He 
also mentioned about contribution of women in different field in s ociety. He further spoke about 
edge India has in terms of diversification, socio economic up  fronts and how Indian society can 
come forward to contribute to take enable India to take the lead i n innovation and technology. He 
highlighted the upward trend seen in IP awareness in India and inc reasing women participation in 
IP. Eminent women speakers who are experts in the field of i ntellectual property and associated 
rights presided over the event. Dr. Sanchita Chaudhary, Vice  president (Projects), Startup 
Incubation and Innovation Centre-IIT Kanpur was the first speaker  of the event. She engaged the 
audience by highlighting the importance of IP and how ecosystem of I P is flourishing  all over the 
world. She mentioned the life term exclusivity of IP. She  drew attention on Publication vs Patent, 
IPR policy and forms of IPR. Er. Sonia Dosanjh, Joint director and Head of AI and Analytics 
Group, Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC), Mohal i portrayed role of 
women as champions in IP since the ancient times. She shared s ome historical examples where 
women have contributed to innovation and technology and IP. Around 150 pa rticipants took part in 
this program, including faculty members, researchers, and stud ents from various institutions from 
Chandigarh and nearby. The session finally culminated with Pr ize Distribution Ceremony organised 
for felicitating winners of essay competition held to generat e awareness regarding IP towards World 
IP Day. Prof Kashmir Singh, Dr Rohini Sharma, Ms. Aparna Ja in and Ms. Harinder Narvan as 
convenors of the event concluded the session with lively discussi on. The objective of the session 
with encouraging innovation and creativity amongst youth was well a ttained.

On

Report 
 
The course was organized by Department of Computer Science and Applications under 
RashtriyaUchchatarShikshaAbhiyan (RUSA) project for  skill enhancement courses in Computer Science and 
Applications. The course coordinators of the worksh op: Dr.Rohini Sharma, Chairperson and Ms. Jasleen K aur 
Bains along with Prof.Sonal Chawla, Principle Inves tigator, RUSA project for Skill enhancement courses  
coordinated this workshop. This course was started as per the mandate of National Education Policy as a step 
towards inculcating skill based education among mas ses as data Science is an upcoming field and people  from 
various areas are using data science concepts in th eir work. For this course more than 300 registratio nsfrom 
different states of the country like, chandigarh, P unjab, Haryana, himachalpradesh, rajasthan, Karnata ka etc. 
were received. More than 100 participants have atte nded this workshop sincerely attending more that 75 % of the 
sessions. This 30 hours workshop was conducted in o nline mode from 4:00 pm to 6:00 pm everyday so that  the 
students and working professionals could attend.  
In the very first session of the workshop, Prof. R. K. Singla talked about Data Science and the need fo r its 
awareness. He discussed the distinction between the  artificial intelligence, machine learning and deep  learning 
in depth and demonstrate different machine learning  models using Google Teachable Machine and Lobe.AI.   
Dr.Rohini Sharma took second session and explained the foundational concepts of Python Programming and  
demonstrate the use of Jupyter notebook with use ca ses and hands on practice as python is the most pop ular 
language among data scientists because of its rich features.  
Ms. Supreet Kaur Mann, Assistant Professor in the d epartment discussed object oriented concepts and th eir 
implementation in python. She further explained the  libraries which are available for use in python.  
Dr.Anuj Kumar, Assistant Professor in the departmen t discussed data visualisation library along with o ther 
libraries like numpy, pandas etc. He explained how different libraries and functions are used in pytho n 
programming for Data visualization. 
Having covered the core concepts and some of the us e-cases of Python programming, it was the perfect t ime to 
move to the domain of machine learning and its appl ications. Prof.Anu Gupta took the session on machin e 
learning and its applications. She emphasized the i mportance of machine learning and how everything is  getting 
in automation these days. Mr. AbhinavKathuria worki ng as assistant professor in RSD College Ferozepur 
further gave practical demonstration of few of its applications. 
The next talk on Data Regression was delivered by P rof. Pradeep Kumar, from Kurukshetra University. Th e 
core concepts were beautifully explained and furthe r he gave practical Demonstration of Data Regressio n 
techniques using Python programming.  
Dr.Anuj Sharma, Assistant Professor in the departme nt delivered a talk on introduction to Data Classif ication 
and techniques. With a pictorial representation, he  illustrated how different fields emerge from AI. T he concept 
of Reinforcement and Transfer learning was also exp lained from mathematical point of view. Mr. Ujjwal,  
working as Assistant Professor on Guest basis demon strated the concepts in python.  
Ms. Supreet Kaur took another session on Data Clust ering and its techniques which is her domain of exp ertise. 
She explained different clustering techniques with practical demonstration. 
Prof.Indu Chhabra delivered talk on Deep learning. She explained the difference of Supervised Learning  and 
unsupervised learning with delightful examples. Pro f. Chhabra related the concepts of deep learning wi th every 
day’s life.Ms. Samita, research scholar in the depa rtment further demonstrated the implementation of t he 
Artificial Neural network using Python programming.  
Dr.Anuj Sharma took an enlightening session on Deep  learning techniques. He explained the working of h idden 
layers, activation functions, inputs and outputs. H e explained the concept of Neural Networks and how the 
results could be optimized by changing weights duri ng back propagation. Further he discussed Convoluti on 
Neural Network.  
Dr.UshaBhadera, Assistant Professor, Jaipuria Insti tute of Management took the session on Data Visuali zation. 
She demonstrated data visualization and its use-cas es using the software Tableau Public. The software was 
indeed of great help as it was easy to use and remo ved the barriers in Microsoft Excel.  
Dr.KavitaTaneja, Assistant Professor in the departm entdelivered a talk on Introduction to Natural Lang uage 
Processing. Dr.Taneja apprised the participants wit h the recent trends of ChatGPT, bard etc. She expla ined the 
steps in Natural Language Processing with practical  implementation. 
After gaining enough knowledge about data science c oncepts, the techniques and practical implementatio n, a 
session on Research Data Analytics and Managing Res earch Data was taken by Dr.Neeraj Kumar Singh, Depu ty 
Librarian, Panjab University. He highlighted the im portance of correct sources of information for the Research 
Scholars and how analysis of Data should be done. H e also underlined the need for managing Research da ta in 
order to alleviate the problems Research Scholars f ace during their research. 
The participants applauded this workshop and reques ted to organized more such workshops on different t opics.  
In this workshop, many people are involved in one w ay or the other to organize it successfully. The fa culty 
members of the department were whole heartedly invo lved in this workshop as most of the sessions have been 
taken by our esteemed and knowledgeable faculty mem bers only. The technical and office staff played th eir part 
really well as no technical glitch has been reporte d throughout the workshop. The external support pro vided by 
computer centre is also well appreciable.The resear ch scholars specially who were part of the organizi ng team 
worked really hard to make this workshop a success:  Arun Sharma, Vaishali, Lalita Thakur and Ujjwal Th akur. 
The excellent feedback received for this workshop m otivated the department to organize more such works hops.

Our Alumni Mr. Saurabh Singh who is currently place d at MediaTek as a Senior Engineer and Mr. 
Arsh Sharma who’s currently placed at Deloitte as A dvisory Analyst, shared their journey at DCSA, 
Panjab University as well as their Journey in the C orporate industry. The session covered the 
following points - 
Sticking to one language, getting command over it a nd also Building those Projects from scratch 
which one can Relate to. 
On top of that mentioning those skills on Resume wh ich is thorough, also they spoke about the 
importance of Practical implementation as well as t heoretical knowledge they always go hand in 
hand.  
They also shared their interview experiences and sh ared how to approach an interviewer with the 
right mindset. They concluded the talk with a doubt  session. 
It was indeed a remarkable session by our Alumni. 
Thank you so much Mr. Saurabh Singh and Mr. Arsh Sh arma for your Guidance and valuable insights. 
We look forward to have more sessions with you.

text:
Department of Computer Science and Applications 
Panjab University, Chandigarh. 
 
One day Symposium  
on  
“Computational Sciences”  
25 th  August, 2022.   
 
 The Department of Computer Science and Application s in collaboration with the Department of 
Statistics organized a one day Symposium on “Comput ational Sciences” on 25 th  August, 2022. The motive of 
the symposium was to highlight the relationship bet ween mathematics, statistics and computer science a nd to 
promote multidisciplinarity as per NEP 2020. The sy mposium started with the inauguration where Dr. Rohi ni 
Sharma, Chairperson Department of Computer Science and Applications and coordinator of the program 
extended welcome to all the dignitaries. She highli ghted the importance of multidisciplinarity to solv e real life 
problems. Coordinator of the program Dr. Manisha fro m Mathematics Department introduced the chief guest  
Prof. B.K. Kuthiyala, Chairman, Haryana State Highe r Education Council and Former Vice-Chancellor MLC 
University, Bhopal. Prof. B.K. Kuthiyala shared his  views on how technology is changing with time and making 
things easier for humans. He shared that technologi es which are coming up every day are being develope d to 
extend the capabilities of human beings but they ar e still not able to match the capabilities of man. Prof. Y. P 
Verma, Registrar Panjab University cited the import ance of Mathematics and Statistics and how these ar eas 
have been complimented by Computer Science. He said  that such programs should be organized regularly f or 
the benefit of our young generation. Prof. Anju Goy al, Chairperson Department of Statistics and coordin ator of 
the program proposed vote of thanks to the chief gu est and other dignitaries. Prof. Kapil K Sharma fro m South 
Asian University explained the relationship between  mathematics and computer science by discussing how  a 
real world problem is solved by converting it into mathematical form and applying computational techni ques. 
Prof. Sandeep Sharma from Guru Nanak Dev University Amritsar discussed ‘Internet of Things’ and its 
applications in agriculture. He mentioned the role of Artificial Intelligence in the Internet of Thing s which can 
solve many complex problems. The declamation contes t on ‘Role of Computational Sciences in the progres s of 
India’ was organized as a part of the symposium whe re students from the department of Computer Science  
and Applications, Mathematics and Statistics shared  their views. Dr. Bharat from University Institute o f Legal 
Studies acted as judge for the declamation contest.  The symposium concluded with valedictory session w here 
participants provided positive and fruitful feedbac k.

Workshop on "Navigating the Job Market Landscape "  
 
On 12 April 2022, , Dr dippy Aggarwal who is curren tly working in Intel 
corporation collaborated with Department of Compute r Science & 
Applications, Panjab University to deliver a sessio n on the above topic.  
 
About the speaker:  
She is an alumnus of DCSA ( batch – 2007),currently  working in Intel 
corporation as a software development engineer. She  is living in America now 
and was on a visit to India.  
 
About the event:  
The session she conducted was on the topic "Navigat ing the Job Market 
Landscape ", wherein she talked about various chall enges she faced when she 
was in our shoes as she also mentioned various poin ts regarding the job 
searching strategies, fear of blanking out in an int erview, how to be prepared 
for the technical interview, how to handle the outc omes of interview like 
rejections and negotiating offers.  
She also mentioned that people look for instant gra tification and also look for 
quick results but the things don't work in that way  as we have to improve our 
skills to beat that benchmark and success is more l ike an iceberg which consists 
a lot more of persistence, dedication to reach that  level. We would like to 
thank her for an enriching, interactive session wit h our students of DCSA.

Panjab University, Chandigarh. 
Report of One Day Workshop on “Copyrights and Relate d Rights” 
A one-day workshop on "Copyrights and Related Rights" was organized by Department of 
Computer Science and Applications, Panjab University, Chandigar h on 25 th  February 2022. 
The Chairperson, Dr. Rohini Sharma delivered the welcome address . After the brief 
introduction about the importance of Copyright by Prof. R.K Singla, t he event started with 
the invited talk of Prof. Rupinder Tewari, IPR Chair, DPI, IIT Chandigarh. It was a well 
illustrated practical delivery about the scope and viability  of Intellectual Property ranging 
from daily usable to our traditional customs. The second expert D r. Neeraj Singh, Deputy 
Librarian, A.C. Joshi Library, Panjab University, Chandigarh de liberated on different kinds 
of Common Creative License boundaries and their importance in the f ield of Academia. The 
talk was demonstrated by the significant advances in thefiel d of exclusive rights. In the third 
session, Professor Rupak Chakravarty, DLIS, Panjab University , Chandigarh shared about 
Open Access Research through Open Educational Resources. The common c reative license 
attributes were well discussed for their aim and boundaries. A ll the three sessions were 
deeply exemplified with the latest practices adopted by the G oggle, YouTube and flip cart. 
The Faculty Members, Research Scholars, Staff Members and st udents made this event an 
open discussion platform by asking queries about how to get intellectua l rights on algorithms 
to final software. In the valedictory session Mrs Anjali Jindia and Dr. Rohini Sharma, 
Chairperson, DCSA, Panjab University, Chandigarh expressed the ir heartfelt thanks to all the 
present dignitaries and participants.

title: c70efa8b2ade1f21
text:
REPORT OF 
TWO DAYS WORKSHOP ON PERSONALITY DEVELOPMENT 
AND SOFT SKILLS  
 
Training and Placement Cell, DCSA conducted 2 Days Workshop in collaboration with Central 
Placement Cell, Panjab University on 10 th  and 11 th  February 2022 .On the first day of workshop 
the first session  was focused on Personality Development  conducted by Dr. Manvinder  .She 
has 19 years of experience in corporate training an d teaching .The session emphasized on the 
steps that could be taken to develop and enhance on e’s personality to make him/her stand out 
from the crowd. She also encouraged the participant s to take up the Myers-Briggs personality 
test and elaborated the 16 personality types. The s ession ended with a fun and engaging activity 
i.e on the spot Story Telling Activity. Personality  Development Session was followed by the 
second session  on Resume  Writing by Prof. Deepti Gupta . She is a professor in the Department 
of English and Cultural Studies with an experience of 36 years. The Resume Writing session 
covered all the nuances of writing a resume wherein  explanation of each and every section of 
resume was covered with minute details. The major d ifferences between CV and resume were 
also addressed. The handouts of the session were al so provided to students which will act as a 
beneficial resource before their interviews.  On th e second day of workshop , Ashish Jain , 
founder of iTinker held a session on  Learning Skills to be Future ready . He talked about the new 
age skills for Gen-Z  like Full Stack Development, Data Science, Block Chain Development, 
Expertise in Metaverse  etc. The workshop concluded  with a session on Interview Skills  by Dr. 
Sanjiv Gupta , Consultant and Industry Expert. He elucidated on the dos and don’ts of an 
interview and how one should present themselves in an interview. Tactics to answer Frequently 
Asked Questions like Strengths, Weaknesses, Why sho uld we hire you? were also touched upon 
by the mentor.  It was the first workshop of the ye ar 2022 conducted successfully by Training 
and Placement Cell. More such workshops will be con ducted in future as well for overall 
development of the students and making them Industr y ready.

Department of Computer Science and Applications 
Panjab University, Chandigarh 
 
One Day Workshop on ‘Machine Learning Techniques’ 
 
REPORT   
 
The Department of Computer Science and Applications, Panjab University , Chandigarh 
organized One Day Workshop on ‘Machine Learning Techniques’ on 4th February  2022. The 
program started with the welcome address by Dr. Rohini Sharma, C hairperson and Coordinator 
of the workshop. She informed that around 300 participants from 15 different s tates of India, 
from industry and from overseas registered for the event. Prof. S. K. Tomar, Dean University 
Instructions talked about the pros and cons of technology in human life. He  expressed that 
machine learning is an emerging area and various developments in t his field will help the current 
and future generations. 
Prof. Tankeshwar Kumar, Hon’ble Vice-Chancellor of the Central Unive rsity of Haryana 
inaugurated the workshop. He linked the idea of machine learning with ast rology and astronomy 
in ancient times where through observations, predictions were made.He shared the idea that 
machine learning has tremendous applications in healthcare, agricul ture, business and many 
other sectors. The predictions made by machines may help us to prote ct our environment, do 
wonders in healthcare to save lives and bring huge changes in the wor ld. The inaugural session 
concluded with the Vote of Thanks delivered by Prof. Indu Chhabra.  
In the first technical session, Prof. Prateek Bhatia, Visiting P rofessor at LAMBDA Lab, at Tel 
Aviv University, Israel and Professor at Thapar Institute of Engi neering and Technology, Patiala, 
discussed about Identification of objects with Deep Learning Techniques . He explained in detail 
the working of Convolutional Neural Network with the description of diff erent steps like 
convolution, max pooling, flattening and full connection. The session ended wit h an interesting 
quiz on the topic covered. 
In the second technical session of the day, Dr. Anuj Sharma, Departme nt of Computer Science & 
Applications, Panjab University,Chandigarh. (Post Doc from RWTH Aache n University, 
Germany) explained Machine Learning based Regression and Class ification techniques like 
linear, polynomial, support vector, decision tree, random forest regre ssion, logistic regression, k-
nearest neighbour, naïve bayes along with implementation. The workshop w as well appreciated 
by the participants.

Chascon -2020  
 
 Panjab Univer sity organized Chandigarh Science Congre ss from 17 -19 December, 
2020. The Departmental events were conducted on 18th December , 2020 . The schedule  
followed and the flyer for December 18, 2020 are given in Annexure – 1 and 2  respectively .  
Prof. A.G. Ramakrishnan, Indian Institute of Science, Bangalore delivered a talk from 
10 to 11.30 am with the following details  
Title: Hard -coded features and DNN.  
Abstract: Human vision is the most sophisticated pattern recognition system known 
to us. Human sensory pathways use very rich, active feedback during the recognition process. 
For example, at the LGN, 31 percent of the synapses are due to feedback from the 
corticothalamic circuits, whereas only 7 percent are due to the inputs from the retinal 
ganglion (feedforward circuits). Similarly, in the auditory pathway, there is active feedback to 
the outer hair cells in the basilar membrane, which in turn modulate th e responses of the 
inner hair cells to the auditory stimuli. Also, attention plays a very important role in visual 
processing and perception by modulating the sensitivity and selectivity. Approximately 30 
participants attended the talk and interacted with the speaker.  
After Prof. A.G. Ramakrishnan’s talk, the following four students and research scholars 
made oral presentations of work done by them.

Webinar Report for  
Building up Happy and Positive Minds during Pandemic times  
                                              
The Department of Computer Science and Applications, Panjab University, Chandigarh 
organized a webinar on ‘ Building up Happy and Positive Minds during 
Pandemic times ’ on November 10th, 2020.  
 
The occasion was graced by Prof. R.K. Singla, Dean of University Instructions, Panjab 
University, Chandigarh, Prof. V.R. Sinha, Dean Research and Dean of University 
Instru ctions(Officiating), Panjab University, Chandigarh, Dr. Balram K. Gupta, Director, 
Chandigarh Judicial Academy, Chandigarh (Guest Speaker), Dr. Rohini Sharma, 
Chairperson, DCSA, Panjab University, Chandigarh and was coordinated by Dr. Indu 
Chhabra, DCSA, P anjab University, Chandigarh and co -coordinated by Ms. Balwinder 
Kaur, Asst. Prof. DCSA, Panjab University, Chandigarh and Ms. Supreet Kaur Mann, 
Asst. Prof. DCSA, Panjab University, Chandigarh.  
The session was overwhelmingly attended by DCSA students, res earch scholars, faculty 
from other departments and colleges too.  
To begin with the webinar,  Prof. R.K Singla  shed light upon the anxiety and pressure 
that this change due to pandemic has brought in our lives. He also shared a few tips to 
stay grounded and relaxed, like taking a moment for being thankful, lifting up your mood 
by doing what interests you, creating and following a relaxed lifestyle and finding  
exercises that can help keep the mind and body in sound state.  
Dr. Balram K. Gupta, the guest speake r, highlighted the key points for building up happy 
and positive minds during pandemic times like covid -19. He shared his thoughts by telling 
a story of a young boy named CORONA where he concluded that in a challenging time 
like this pandemic what matters most is how you handle the situation. He highlighted the 
points to change our mindset in an optimistic way so that we can think, feel and know 
how to face challenges. He also spread a light on positive outcomes of this aspect by 
praising the advancement of  technology and improvement in one’s skill by interacting 
globally during this pandemic. By these sayings he concluded that there is no substitute 
for physical interaction is a myth and an outcome of a sick mindset, only cultivated happy 
minds can understa nd that there is an alternative for physical interactions i.e technology. 
He said that excellence must be the goal of youth and the recipe he shared to experience 
happiness is by doing our best, believing and thinking positive and feeling happy about 
that, as happiness is human right.  
He also focused upon nurturing good values to keep ourselves happy and not letting them 
get devalued. With the increasing domestic violence, murders and crimes in the society, 
cultivating and nurturing happy minds is necessary , he added. He also cited the 
importance of Bhakti in our lives to control anger and cultivate happy minds and positive 
vibes. At last, he concluded that a positive mind leads to a creative mind.  
Prof. V.R. Sinha  through his thoughts focused upon what matt ers is a persons’ attitude 
in such hard and testing situations. And how with a humble start and a positive attitude 
and mindset one can reach the zenith of success.  
To summarize, the session  was very interactive, full of various enriching stories and an 
amalgamation of thoughts and positivity of  Dr. Balram K. Gupta.

Webinar Report for  
NEP 2009/2020: Open Standards For Interactive Computing  
                                              
The Department of Computer Science and Applications, Panjab University Chandigarh 
organized a webinar on ‘ NEP 2009/2020: Open Standards For Interactive Computing ’ 
on October 15th, 2020.  
 
The occasion was graced by Prof. V.R. Sinha, Dean Research and officiating  Dean of 
University Instructions, Panjab University Chandigarh , Prof. Maninder Singh, Head of 
Compu ter Science and Engineering Department and Center of Information and 
Technology Management (CITM), Thapar Institute of Engineering and Technology, 
Patiala(Guest Speaker), Dr. Rohini Sharma, Chairperson, DCSA, Panjab University, 
Chandigarh and was coordinat ed by Prof. Sonal Chawla, DCSA, Panjab University, 
Chandigarh.  
The session was overwhelmingly attended by DCSA students, research scholars, faculty 
from other departments and colleges too.  
Prof. V.R Sinha  highlighted upon the mandate of NEP 2020 which is t o make the 
education system holistic and multidisciplinary and encourage the use of technology for 
effective teaching.  
He dwelled upon the changes proposed by the policy which were : - Multiple entry and 
Multiple exits, abolishment of M.Phil, autonomy which  could be given to private colleges, 
one regulator for higher education and parity between the government and private 
colleges.  
He also threw light upon some of the challenges such as the problem with wet labs for 
subjects like chemistry and physics which requires contact. Its solution could be 
development of virtual labs.  
 
Prof. Maninder Singh, the guest speaker,  highlighted the importance of quality 
education which can only be achieved through a strong framework and design. Various 
important points of the  NEP like adopting a 5+3+3+4 model  for school education starting 
at age 3 , which recognises the primacy of the formative years from ages 3 to 8 in shaping 
the child’s future.  
He also focused on 2009’s Right to Education in the Constitution of India which p rovided 
free and compulsory education for all children in the age group of six to fourteen years as 
a Fundamental Right.  
He emphasised on quality education and virtual labs and the change in the overall 
spending of the government from 3% of the GDP to prop osed 6% of the GDP on the 
national education, and the key aspect of measurement such as international rankings 
and research aspect.  
 
He vividly explained the importance of Google Colaboratory  and Project 
Jupyter (Project Jupyter exists to develop open -sourc e software, open -standards, and 
services for interactive computing across dozens of programming languages)  through 
interactive examples and great explanation.  
 
To summarize, the session  was very interactive, enriching and an amalgamation of 
thoughts and ex pertise of  Prof. Maninder Singh, Thapar Institute of Engineering and 
Technology, Patiala, and all the topics were profoundly presented and explained along 
with the apparent doubts being unraveled.

text:
Webinar Report for  
National Educational Policy 2020: Introducing Coding at young age  
 
September 25th, 2020 was marked as another informative day as a webinar was 
organized on ‘ National Education Policy 2020 : Introducing Coding at young age ’ by 
Department of Computer Science and Applications, Panjab University Chandigarh and 
Vidya Bharti.  
The webinar marked the presence of eminent personalities like Sh. Vijay Nadda, 
Organising Secretary North -India, Vidya Bharti (Chief Guest), Prof Raj Kuma r, Hon'ble 
Vice-Chancellor Panjab University Chandigarh (Chief Patron), Prof R. K. Singla, Dean 
University Instruction Panjab University Chandigarh (Patron), Prof Sanjeev K. Sofat, CSE, 
PEC, Chandigarh (Speaker) and was coordinated by Dr. Rohini Sharma, Ch airperson 
(Officiating), DCSA, Panjab University, Chandigarh and was attended by teachers, 
research scholars, school Principals, teachers and students.  
About the webinar:  
The webinar began with the enlightening speech by Prof Raj Kumar, Hon'ble Vice -
Chance llor Panjab University Chandigarh, in which he shed light upon the significance of 
learning to code at an early age to help in self -growth as well as of the society and make 
the dream of our Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Atma Nirbhar Bharat a success.  
 
Further in the webinar, Sh. Vijay Nadda, Organising Secretary North -India, Vidya Bharti, 
our Chief Guest, shared his enlightening words about the new ‘Shiksha Neeti’ and how it 
marks an important step by the government to help brighten the future of the nat ion. He 
also mentioned the role of a good teacher in shaping the student’s future, as it is the 
teacher whose hand the student holds in his journey to success.  
 
Further Prof. Sanjeev talked about  the National Education Policy 2020 in brief and how 
the cha nges and the new schemes added by the Government in the Education Policy 
helps to enhance the educational quality. The key note of the policy is that the 
Government decided to introduce coding to students at a young age. They will start doing 
and learning the concept of coding from 6th Grade which will work as a boon for the 
students who like to work in fields like Artificial Intelligence and Robotics in future.  
After that he explained how this decision  is beneficial to every individual and specially for 
kids. The following advantages for the same are:  
i). Coding helps in problem solving and it will increase the learning capacity to           
understand the concepts in a better way.  
ii).  Kids learn how things work in the real world at an early age.  
iii). T his will lead to algorithmic and structural thinking in kids, that is, they will get the 
ability to define clear steps to solve a problem and how problems can be solved efficiently 
by dividing it into smaller modules.  
iv). Students will learn perseverance,  that is , doing something despite difficulty or delay 
in work.  
v). Coding concepts produce a habit of curiosity and will push the students to ask 
questions.  
vi).  Students will learn to observe and analyze things in a better way.  
vii).  Coding shows mathe matics in action and helps them to learn in a broader way.  
 
Despite so many benefits of introducing coding to kids, there are some challenges as well 
to implement it in a perfect way.  
 
Some of the major Challenges which can be faced are following :  
 
i). La ck of Infrastructure : In India, the ratio of  children to computers is low which will lead 
to difficulty for the students. Also, the Internet connectivity is a major issue as it is difficult 
for the students to access the Internet who live in villages and  small towns.  
 
ii). Quality Teachers : Coding is a conceptual and practical subject so it's the need of the 
hour that it should be taught by those who know about it and who can explain it in such a 
way that students will not get scared at first.Younger tea cher can get it easily as they 
have the better ability to go through it.  
 
At last, our speaker Prof. Sanjeev Sofat concluded that this new policy can prove to be 
helpful if we overcome the challenges and it will  lead to a bright future for the students.  
 
Finally, Dr. Parminder Duggal, Principal, Ankur School, Chandigarh, in her speech again 
highlighted the importance of learning to code as it improved confidence and helped 
students to think out of the box. She found coding so important that she wanted to g ive it 
a try herself.  
 
To sum up, the webinar was a really informative one and helped equip everyone with the 
benefits and need of learning to code from a very young age.  
 
 
 
Compiled  by: 
Bhuvan Thakur and Manandeep Kaur  
MCA 3rd Semester(Morning)

text:
Depar tment of Computer Science and Applications  
 
Webinar Report  
 
National Educational Policy 2020: Introducing Coding at young age  
 
September 25th, 2020 was marked as another informative day as a webinar was 
organized on ‘ National Education Policy 2020 : Introducing Coding at young age ’ 
by Department of Computer Science and Applications, Panjab University Chandigarh 
and Vidya Bharti.  
The webinar marked the presence of eminent personalities like Sh. Vijay Nadda, 
Organising Secretary North -India, Vidya Bharti (Chief Guest), Prof Raj Kuma r, Hon'ble 
Vice-Chancellor Panjab Unive rsity Chandigarh (Chief Patron) and  Prof Sanjeev K. 
Sofat, CSE, PEC, Chandigarh (Speaker) . The event was coordinated by Dr. Rohini 
Sharma, Ch airperson (Officiating), DCSA, Panjab University, Chandigarh and was 
attended by teachers, research schola rs, school Pr incipals and students.  
About the webinar:  
The webinar began with the welcome address by Dr. Rohini Sharma where she 
discussed that coding is a basic literacy in this digital age and this idea of  introducing 
coding at young age can be achieved by joint efforts of all the stakeholders. Prof Raj 
Kumar, Hon'ble Vice -Chance llor Panjab University Chandigarh, gave an enlightening 
speech where he shed light upon the significance of learning to code at an early age to 
help in self -growth as well as of the society and make the dream of our Prime Minister 
Narendra Modi’s Atma Nirbhar Bharat a success.  
 
Further in the webinar, Sh. Vijay Nadda, Organising Secretary North -India, Vidya Bharti, 
our Chief Guest, shared his enlightening words about the new ‘Shiksha Neeti’ and how 
it marks an important step by the government to help brighten the future of the nat ion. 
He also mentioned the role of a good teacher in shaping the student’s future, as it is the 
teacher whose hand the student holds in his journey to success.  
 
Further Prof. Sanjeev  Sofat  talked about  the National Education Policy 2020 in brief 
and how the cha nges and the new schemes added by the Government in the Education 
Policy helps to enhance the educational quality. The key note of the policy is that the 
Government decided to introduce coding to students at a young age. They will start 
doing and learning the concept of coding from 6th Grade which will work as a boon for 
the students who like to work in fields like Artificial Intelligence and Robotics in future.  
After that he explained how this decision  is beneficial to every individual and specially to 
kids. He talked about the following advantages : 
i). Coding helps in problem solving and it will increase the learning capacity to           
understand the concepts in a better way.  
ii).  Kids learn how things work in the real world at an early age.  
iii). T his will lead to algorithmic and structural thinking in kids, that is, they will get the 
ability to define clear steps to solve a problem and how problems can be solved 
efficiently by dividing it into smaller modules.  
iv). Students will learn perseverance,  that is,  doing something despite difficulty or delay 
in work.  
v). Coding concepts produce a habit of curiosity and will push the students to ask 
questions.  
vi).  Students will learn to observe and analyze things in a better way.  
vii).  Coding shows mathe matics in action and helps them to learn in a broader way.  
 
Despite so many benefits of introducing coding to kids, there are some challenges as 
well to implement it in a perfect way.  
 
Some of the major Challenges w hich can be faced are as follows : 
 
i). La ck of Infrastructure : In India, the ratio of  children to computers is low which will 
lead to difficulty for the students. Also, the Internet connectivity is a major issue as it is 
difficult for the students to access the Internet who live in villages and  small towns.  
 
ii). Quality Teachers : Coding is a conceptual and practical subject so it's the need of the 
hour that it should be taught by those who know about it and who can explain it in such 
a way that students will not get scared at first.  Younger tea cher can get it easily as they 
have the better ability to go through it.  
 
At last, our speaker Prof. Sanjeev Sofat concluded that this new policy can prove to be 
helpful if we overcome the challenges and it will  lead to a bright future for the students.  
 
Finally, Dr. Parminder Duggal, Principal, Ankur School, Chandigarh, expressed her 
views on the topic. She highlighted the importance of learning to code as it improves 
confidence and helps  students to think out of the box. She found coding so important 
that she wanted to g ive it a try herself.  
 
To sum up, the webinar was  really  an informative one and helped equip everyone with 
the benefits and need of learning to code from a very young age.

PRESS NOTE 
"Turning Waste into Wonder” - Best Out of Waste Eve nt Organized by DCSA, Panjab 
University 
The Department of Computer Science and Applications  (DCSA) at Panjab University, in 
collaboration with the Swachh Bharat Abhiyan initia tive, organized an inspiring "Best Out of 
Waste" event on 30 August 2024. The event was a joi nt effort between Dr.Anuj Gupta, the 
coordinator of Swachh Bharat Abhiyan, and Dr.Kavita Taneja, the event coordinator from 
DCSA, aimed at promoting creativity and environment al awareness among students by 
encouraging them to transform waste materials into useful and artistic items. 
 
The event began with an introduction to the Swachh Bharat Abhiyan and its significance, 
highlighting the importance of waste management and  sustainability. The main event saw 
enthusiastic participation from students, who prese nted a wide variety of projects made 
from everyday waste items, showcasing their creativ ity and commitment to the cause. 
 
Participants engaged in a friendly competition wher e their projects were evaluated based on 
creativity, innovation, and effective use of waste materials. Highlights included decorative 
wall art made from discarded CDs, functional lamps crafted from plastic bottles, Wind mill 
using paper cuttings based on the Principles of Sci ence, Wind chime made from paper cups 
and threads symbolizing good fortune and good luck for the new students to start their new 
journey in DCSA and beautiful idols using plastic b ottles, newspapers and cardboard, 
reflecting the student’s ingenuity. 
 
Dr.Anuj Sharma,the chairperson of DCSA, delivered a n inspiring speech on the significance 
of sustainable living, emphasizing the need to redu ce waste and embrace eco-friendly 
practices. Dr.KavitaTaneja, also addressed the stud ents, highlighting significance of this 
event in finding sustainable solution for waste man agement and to sensitize the students to 
feel the responsibility towards the environment.  
 
The event concluded with a prize distribution cerem ony, recognizing the top projects for 
their outstanding creativity and innovation. Certif icates of appreciation were awarded to all 
participants and volunteers.  
 
This "Best Out of Waste" event at DCSA not only sho wcased the potential of discarded 
materials but also inspired participants to adopt s ustainable practices, reinforcing the 
message that creativity can drive change towards a cleaner, greener future.
